buyer_added_terms.text: 1. Generic OPTION CLAUSE: The Purchaser reserves the right to increase or decrease the quantity to be ordered up to 25 percent of bid quantity at the time of placement of contract. The purchaser also reserves the right to increase the ordered quantity up to 25% of the contracted quantity during the currency of the contract at the contracted rates. The delivery period of quantity shall commence from the last date of original delivery order and in cases where option clause is exercised during the extended delivery period the additional time shall commence from the last date of extended delivery period. The additional delivery time shall be (Increased quantity ÷ Original quantity) × Original delivery period (in days), subject to minimum of 30 days. If the original delivery period is less than 30 days, the additional time equals the original delivery period. The Purchaser may extend this calculated delivery duration up to the original delivery period while exercising the option clause. Bidders must comply with these terms. 2. Generic Experience Criteria: The Bidder or its OEM {themselves or through reseller(s)} should have regularly, manufactured and supplied same or similar Category Products to any Central / State Govt Organization / PSU for 3 years before the bid opening date. Copies of relevant contracts to be submitted along with bid in support of having supplied some quantity during each of the year. In case of bunch bids, the primary product having highest value should meet this criterion.

3. Turnover Bidder Turn Over Criteria: The minimum average annual financial turnover of the bidder during the last three years, ending on 31st March of the previous financial year, should be as indicated in the bid document. Documentary evidence in the form of certified Audited Balance Sheets of relevant periods or a certificate from the Chartered Accountant / Cost Accountant indicating the turnover details for the relevant period shall be uploaded with the bid. In case the date of constitution / incorporation of the bidder is less than 3 year old, the average turnover in respect of the completed financial years after the date of constitution shall be taken into account for this criteria. 4. Turnover OEM Turn Over Criteria: The minimum average annual financial turnover of the OEM of the offered product during the last three years, ending on 31st March of the previous financial year, should be as indicated in the bid document. Documentary evidence in the form of certified Audited Balance Sheets of relevant periods or a certificate from the Chartered Accountant / Cost Accountant indicating the turnover details for the relevant period shall be uploaded with the bid. In case the date of constitution / incorporation of the OEM is less than 3 year old, the average turnover in respect of the completed financial years after the date of constitution shall be taken into account for this criteria. In case of bunch bids, the OEM of CATEGORY RELATED TO primary product having highest bid value should meet this criterion. 5. Certificates Bidder's offer is liable to be rejected if they don't upload any of the certificates / documents sought in the Bid document, ATC and Corrigendum if any. 6. Certificates To be eligible for award of contract, Bidder / OEM must possess following Certificates / Test Reports on the date of bid opening (to be uploaded with bid): YES . 7. Buyer Added Bid Specific ATC Buyer Added text based ATC clauses 1. The procurement of supplementary nutrition shall be made in accordance with Rule 149 of GFR,2017 , the Finance Department Circular dated 25-0 8-2025 , SNA-SPARSH guidelines , and the Governemnt of India’s Mission Saksham Anganwadi & Poshan 2.0 procurement guidelines . 2. All codal formalities shall be observed as per the provisions laid down in t he General Financial Rules (GFR) 2017, as amended from time to time. 3. The funds shall be utilized strictly after fulfillment of requisite codal/proce dural formalities required under the rules/norms. 4 . The product should have a detailed description, including required nutritional values, packaging, batch numbers, manufacturing and expiry dates, and all statutory details. 5. No diversion or re-appropriation of funds shall be made under any circums tances. 6. The items supplied must conform to the specified standards and specifica tion. 7. The procurement shall be made within the available budget, ensuring tha

t no liabilities are created and financial discipline is maintained in letter and spirit. 8. The supplying agency must supply the nutrition items as per the approve d specification of the items, and the Brand must be FSSAI- ceritified / ap proved/fortified Grade-I, with no compromise on the quality and specific ations of the nutrition items. 9. The rates should be inclusive of all taxes, transportation, and associated c harges, including freight charges up to the Angawadi centre level,as the supplier(S) shall deliver the supplies to the Anganwadi centres under pro per receipt as per indent. 10. At the time of supply, items must have a shelf life of six months, except f or those items having an approved shelf life below six months (wherein t he maximum approved period shall be considered) from the date of rece ipt at the Anganwadi level. 11. A fine shall be imposed pursuant to the Food Safety and Standards Act o f India and rules made thereunder, up to the maximum amount, if any vi olation of norms and quality is fund at any stage. 12. The risk of loss generally transfers to the buyer upon acceptance of goo ds at the delivery point. 13. The supplier must adhere to all applicable local, state, and federal laws and regulations, including labor laws and non-discrimination policies, ens uring open and free competition. 14. The supplying agency should have premised/shops for pre-procurement inspection, during procurement, and for inspections of quality/quantity o f all nutritional items at any stage of procurement. 15. A Bank Guarantee or Security Deposit of 2 % of the contracted value sha ll be deposited, which shall be released three months after successful co mpletion of supplies at the Anganwadi Centre(s)level,it shall be forfeited if the supplier fails to deliver the supply within the specified period or if t he suuplies are found substandard. 16. Nutrition items should be supplied to AWCS within seven (7) days of rec eiving the supply order/contract as per GeM rules. 17. The supplier(s) shold not under liquidation, court receivership, or similar proceedings and should not be bankrupt. 18. The supplier (s) shall supply nutritional items along with a quality certifi cate, and random testing of nutrition items will be conducted by the Foo d Safety Department at any stage. 19. The supplier (s) must hold a valid FSSAI License, Trade Certificate/licenc e, and GST Registration in nutritional items . In addition for Co-operative s, a Registration certificate, approved by-laws and a functionality certific ate from the concerned competent authority are required. 20. The procurement shall be made within the available budget, ensuring th

at no liabilities are created and financial discipline shall be maintained in letter and spirit. 21. The supplier(s) should submit an affidavit, duly attested by a Judicial Ma gistrate, stating that the firm/supplying agency (Super Bazar/Co-operativ es,Stores, fixed price shops/Registered local shopkeepers and others) is not blacklisted by any Govt or Semi- Govt authority. 22. The supplier (s) warrants that the goods conform to descriptions, are fre e from defects, are of satisfactory quality, and fit for the intended purpos e (Human consumption). 23. This office reserves the right to accept/ reject or withdrawal/cancel the contract with specific reason(s). 24. A pre Bid Meeting shall be held to thoroughly explain the Nutritional Spe cification, delivery mechanism and documentation. 25. Bidder shall submit 1 kg/1 Ltr sample of each Quoted items before techn ical evaluation , failure to submit sample shall lead to rejection of bid. . 8.
